title: New program: $10m Fund for Multi-Agent Safety (Cooperative AI Foundation / Schmidt Sciences / Google DeepMind / ARIA / Google.org)
summary: CAIF's own site lists a call for proposals for a $10M Fund for Multi-Agent Safety, co-funded with Schmidt Sciences, Google DeepMind, the Advanced Research + Invention Agency (ARIA), and Google.org. It funds 1-2 year research grants on safety risks from large-scale multi-agent AI systems (emergent collective dynamics, trustworthy agent interaction infrastructure, monitoring/control for complex multi-agent networks), in two tiers: up to $300,000 and $300,000-$1,000,000. Deadline August 8, 2026, 11:59 PM AoE; applications managed through Schmidt Sciences' portal. This program is not currently in registry/programs (only cooperative-ai-phd-fellowship and cooperative-ai-research-grants exist for this org).

title: New program: Mozilla Foundation Incubator (Build/Sustain tracks) missing from registry/programs
summary: Mozilla's own grantmaking hub (mozillafoundation.org/en/what-we-do/grantmaking/) currently lists four active programs: Incubator, Mozilla Fellows, Responsible Computing Challenge, and Collaborative Funds. The Mozilla Technology Fund (already in registry/programs) is absent from that list. The Incubator program is not in the registry at all: it funds values-driven tech projects (climate impacts, AI and democracy, data transparency, algorithmic accountability) via two tracks -- Build Track (prototype-to-product-community-fit) and Sustain Track (proven tech to long-term sustainability) -- with mentorship, workshops, and MozFest visibility. Current cohorts referenced on the page: 'Democracy x AI Cohort' and '2025 Cohort: Making the invisible visible.' No award size or apply deadline is listed on the page; interested parties sign up for notifications when new calls for proposals open.

title: Chainlink Community Grant Program not discoverable on any current site page checked
summary: The existing profile already hedges that 'the grant program is not referenced on the current homepage.' This pass independently checked chain.link/ (homepage), chain.link/community, and chain.link/blog (blog.chain.link/tag/grants/ now 301-redirects here) -- none of the three reference a Community Grant Program, past or current; the only grant-adjacent content found was a hackathon ('Convergence: A Chainlink Hackathon'). This doesn't confirm the program is dead (it may simply not be linked from top-level nav), but three independent checks turning up nothing raises the question of whether it's still running. Recommend the owner spot-check via a direct search or Chainlink Labs contact before the profile continues asserting an active Community Grant Program.

title: EtherFi is tagged roles:[funder] but its own site describes no third-party grant or funding program
summary: ether.fi's homepage describes only protocol features for its own users (restaking products, Cash card, TVL stats) plus a bug bounty (Immunefi) and governance/DAO mechanics -- no grants, ecosystem fund, or funding program for external builders is mentioned anywhere on the page. This is the same pattern flagged for EleutherAI in an earlier batch: roles:[funder] without an evidenced funding mechanism. Recommend downgrading roles to ecosystem, or sourcing a specific ether.fi grants program if one exists elsewhere (e.g. governance forum proposals), before continuing to list it as a funder.

title: Thinking Machines Lab is tagged roles:[funder] but its own site describes no grants or funding program
summary: thinkingmachines.ai describes itself as an AI research and product company; the page commits to publishing research and sharing code/datasets/model specs to 'accelerate external research,' but nowhere mentions grants, funding, or a program for external applicants. Existing profile text already notes this ('does not mention any grants or external funding programs'). Recommend downgrading roles to ecosystem unless a grant program can be sourced.

title: Protocol Labs' funding brand may be shifting to 'PL R&D' (plrd.org) -- relationship to existing protocol-labs-research program unclear
summary: protocol.ai now features 'PL R&D' at plrd.org alongside 'PL Capital' (plcapital.xyz) as its current funding-adjacent brands, with focus areas (Digital Human Rights, Economies & Governance, AI & Robotics, Neurotechnology) that overlap with but aren't identical to the existing protocol-labs-research program's framing (RFPs, open research awards, fellowships; status: paused since 2023). PL R&D's own page describes itself as a 'coordination layer' rather than a traditional grant program, and does not state whether it supersedes, replaces, or runs alongside the paused Research Grants program. Not confident enough to fact-fill or auto-merge; flagging for the owner to determine whether PL R&D is the rebrand of protocol-labs-research (in which case status should probably change from paused) or a genuinely separate initiative.
